chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Maymun, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) arrived in a state of Tamattu' — on the night of 'Arafah he performed Tawaf, then released himself from Ihram, and visited some of his female slaves, then he entered Ihram for Hajj and departed.

key_terms.أَهَلَّ بِالْحَجِّ: He entered Ihram for Hajj (re-consecrating for the pilgrimage)
key_terms.فَطَافَ: He performed Tawaf (circumambulation of the Kaaba)
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ عَرَفَةَ: The night of 'Arafah (the night before the Day of 'Arafah)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعًا: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah and Hajj separately with a release of Ihram in between)
key_terms.وَأَحَلَّ: And he released himself from Ihram (ending the state of consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual procedure for the Tamattu' Hajj as practiced by the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides a foundational precedent for the Shia jurisprudence of Hajj al-Tamattu', demonstrating the Imam's authority to perform the Umrah and Hajj as distinct rites. By entering Ihram for Hajj on the night of 'Arafah after completing Umrah, the Imam illustrates the flexibility and validity of delaying the Ihram for Hajj until the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, a key distinction in Shia fiqh compared to other schools.
